correctness.rationale: Subtracting the coordinate center-valued traces gives an equivalent exact trace-zero representative. Wang’s uniform theorem factors every coordinate as one commutator with a universal product bound; reciprocal rescaling makes both factor sequences bounded. The converse, quotient norm identity, and trace-space factorization follow from traciality and contractivity of the center-valued trace.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Wang’s 2026 theorem does not state the operator-norm reduced-product or ultraproduct consequence. Hardy covers unique trace and self-adjoint self-commutators in pseudomatricial settings, but the arbitrary-element single-commutator kernel with universal norm control and arbitrary finite-von-Neumann reduced-product formulation were not located.

value.rationale: The theorem turns the set of single commutators into an explicitly identified closed linear subspace, computes the corresponding quotient isometrically as the reduced product of centers, and classifies all tracial states. For norm ultraproducts of finite factors this yields a closed codimension-one commutator hyperplane with the same universal coordinate bound.
